introduction: Today we celebrate the birth of Saint John the Baptist. He is one of very few saints whose birth the Church celebrates, because he was sanctified before his birth for his mission as the forerunner of Christ. Isaiah speaks of a servant called from the womb; Paul recalls John's witness to Jesus. In the Gospel, Zechariah writes, His name is John, and his tongue is freed. Let us give thanks for the gift of every life and for our own calling.

prayerOfTheFaithful.invitation: Brothers and sisters, God called John from his mother's womb to prepare the way of the Lord. Let us bring our prayers to the Father.
intentions: For the Church: that, like John the Baptist, she may point beyond herself to Christ, the Lamb of God. Let us pray to the Lord.
For parents and families awaiting the birth of a child: that every child may be welcomed as a gift from God. Let us pray to the Lord.
For all who are called to prepare the way for Christ in difficult places: that God may give them courage. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those who have lost their voice or their hope: that God may open their mouths to praise him again. Let us pray to the Lord.
For ourselves: that we may discover the purpose for which God formed us and follow it faithfully. Let us pray to the Lord.
prayerOfTheFaithful.conclusion: Father, you called Saint John the Baptist to prepare a people for your Son. By his prayers, help us to point others to Christ and to walk in the way of salvation. Through Christ our Lord.

reflection.title: What then will this child be?
reflection.body:
The Church usually celebrates saints on the day of their death, their birth into heaven. Only for Jesus, Mary and John the Baptist do we celebrate the day of their earthly birth. John is honored in this way because, from his mother's womb, he was chosen for a unique mission: to prepare the way for the Messiah.

The first reading could have been written for him: "the LORD has called me from the womb; from the inside of my mother, he has mentioned my name." The psalm sings the same wonder for every human life: "You knit me together in my mother's womb. I will give thanks to you, for I am fearfully and wonderfully made."

The Gospel tells of John's birth and naming. The neighbors want to call him Zechariah, after his father. But Elizabeth says, "Not so; but he will be called John." Zechariah, who had been struck mute for doubting the angel, asks for a tablet and writes, "His name is John." At once "His mouth was opened immediately and his tongue freed, and he spoke, blessing God." The people ask, "What then will this child be?"

Paul, in the second reading, tells us what he became. John preached repentance and then pointed away from himself: "I am not he. But behold, one comes after me, the sandals of whose feet I am not worthy to untie." His greatness lay in his humility.

The same question can be asked of every child, and of each of us: what will this child be? God has a purpose for every life. This week, give thanks for the gift of your own life, and ask the Lord how you can prepare the way for Christ in the lives of others.
